title: doctor's gate check tests the carrier for a guard runner the shim never names, so every v3 estate reports GateNotRunning while its guards run
body:
`doctor`'s gate check decides whether guards run by testing whether the **carrier** text contains the literal string `pre-commit-guards.sh`. That premise held for the monolithic carrier and is false for the shim carrier `canon` now installs, so **every estate that moves to v3 is reported as running no guards, actionably, while its guards run.** Conflab is the first, as of its hoist on 2026-08-28.

## The mechanism

`native/rust/crates/intentsvcs/src/doctor.rs:1086`:

```rust
if !carrier.contains("pre-commit-guards.sh") {
  return GateState::CarrierRunsNoGuards;
}
```

`CarrierRunsNoGuards` is the Baize state and surfaces as `FindingClass::GateNotRunning`, which this file's own doc comment classes as **ACTIONABLE** rather than advisory -- a red an operator is told to act on.

But `canon::install_carrier` (`canon.rs:497-500`) writes `lib/templates/hooks/pre-commit-shim.sh` to `<hooks>/pre-commit.intent`. **The shim names no guard runner by design.** It resolves `~/.intent/home` and execs the gate; the gate is what reaches the runner. Measured on Conflab immediately after its hop:

| file | `pre-commit-guards.sh` | `GUARD_RUNNER` | `intent/home` |
| ---- | ---------------------- | -------------- | ------------- |
| Conflab carrier (shim, 7332 b, `b0ed7edd`) | **0** | **0** | 2 |
| the gate it execs (`pre-commit.sh`, 34701 b) | **6** | **4** | 0 |
| Devbin carrier (monolithic, 20899 b, `ae5d0695`) | 3 | 4 | 0 |

The chain resolves end to end: dispatcher (`chain block`, mode `-rwxr-xr-x`) -> shim -> `state: OK`, `root: /Users/matts/Devel/prj/Intent`, `gate: lib/templates/hooks/pre-commit.sh`.

Predicate for every cell: `grep -c '<single literal>' <file>`, run **once per column**. Stated because the first version of this table did not state it, and was wrong for exactly that reason -- see the correction note at the foot.

The chain resolves end to end: dispatcher (`chain block`, mode `-rwxr-xr-x`) -> shim -> `state: OK`, `root: /Users/matts/Devel/prj/Intent`, `gate: lib/templates/hooks/pre-commit.sh`.

The check's own comment states the premise it now violates: *"the marker is the guard runner the carrier MUST REACH"*. Under the shim the carrier reaches the **gate**, and the gate reaches the runner. **The architecture moved and the check did not.**

## The second defect, which is the worse one

`doctor.rs:1203-1205` reads the comparison template from `lib/templates/hooks/pre-commit.sh` -- **the gate** -- while `install_carrier` writes `hooks/pre-commit-shim.sh` to the carrier path. Different files, so `template != carrier` is **permanently true** for a shim estate and it reports `BehindTheTemplate` forever.

**Fixing only the guard check leaves the estate red anyway.** This file already argues against exactly that outcome, a few lines below the check:

> a check that reds every estate in the fleet permanently is one operators learn to skip, and a skipped check is not there for the two estates that are actually broken either

## Why this is worse than a cosmetic false positive

1. It fires on the command everyone runs, on the estates that just did the thing they were asked to do. **The reward for adopting v3 is a red gate report.**
2. **0065 compounds it**: `doctor` has no acknowledgement mechanism, so a shim estate cannot silence a red it knows is wrong. Permanent, unsuppressible, and wrong.
3. It is a **false RED on a false-green detector**. This check exists because Baize was silently unprotected. An operator who learns to skip it loses the check for the estate that really is broken -- which is the failure the check was written to prevent, reintroduced from the other side.

## What would settle it

`gate_state` is a pure function, deliberately separated from its IO so every arm can be driven -- this file says so explicitly. **A test feeding it the shim body should therefore be cheap**, and would fail today.

**I did not run it.** This report is from reading the source, plus two independent measurements of Conflab's post-hop carrier taken by different nodes with different instruments. A build was barred in the Intent tree during the hoist and lifting that bar was not mine to assume. **So: confirmed by reading, not by execution, and the distinction is deliberate.**

## Not proposed

No fix is proposed here. Whether the discriminator becomes "follow the pointer and test what the gate reaches", or the shim gains a marker, or `gate_state` learns the two carrier shapes, is a design call with fleet-wide reach and it belongs to whoever owns the gate's architecture -- not to a reporting node from another estate.

---

Reported by devbin/cc at hv's direct instruction, from Devbin. Conflab's post-hop state measured read-only at 2026-08-28 12:09Z; carrier `b0ed7edd...`, byte-identical to `pre-commit-shim.sh` read in the same command.

## Correction, 2026-08-28, by the filer

**The gate row first read `9 | 9` and both cells were wrong.** Caught by devbin/vc, who could not reproduce it with three independent counters and said so.

`9` was a real number answering a question this table does not ask. It came from `grep -cE 'GUARD_RUNNER|pre-commit-guards\.sh'` -- **an alternation, so it counts LINES MATCHING EITHER pattern**, and it was then written into **both** per-pattern columns. The arithmetic closes exactly: 6 + 4 - 1 line matching both = 9. Conflab's `0 | 0 | 2` and Devbin's `3 | 4 | 0` reproduce unchanged; only this row moved.

**No conclusion in this issue depended on it.** 6 and 4 are non-zero, so the gate still reaches the runner and every argument above stands. **That is precisely why it is recorded rather than quietly fixed:** a wrong number underneath a right answer has no trigger for re-inspection, because the answer keeps looking correct.

**It is also the second instance of one defect in fifteen minutes.** The same alternation-as-a-per-item-count error produced a `guard refs 2` reading in the filer's own verification run, which was found, disclosed and written up -- and then reproduced here, in a HIGH issue another estate would implement from. **Fixing the instance did not prevent the habit.** The durable form is the rule now stated above the table: one literal per column, never an alternation, and the predicate printed beside the number.

## Folded in from 0107 and 0108 (intent-dc, 2026-08-28, on intent-vc's ruling)

**0108 was a straight duplicate of this issue and is closed into it. 0107 is closed into it too, and its devbin half was FALSE** -- see the correction at the foot.

### A second-tree instance of the carrier executing guards

The carrier this issue reports as running no guards has been measured running them on **two trees, by two runs, under two HOMEs**:

- the real hop's commit in Conflab printed `guards: 4 ran, 0 skipped`;
- the **Phase 1.1 rehearsal** commit printed the same line hours earlier, on an `rsync -a` filesystem copy, **under a decoy `HOME`**, over a byte-identical carrier (`b0ed7edd`, 7332 b, mode 711 / `-rwx--x--x`).

The decoy arm adds something the real-tree arm cannot: **the shim's guard execution does not depend on the real `~/.intent/`.** A seeded pointer resolved it identically, so the failure is in the check's premise and not in any property of this machine's install.

### The specification sits one line above the bug

`doctor.rs:1065`, the variant's own doc comment:

```rust
/// Installed, running, and older than the template it was copied from.
BehindTheTemplate { carrier: usize, template: usize },
```

**"the template it was copied from" is exactly right and exactly what the check does not do.** A shim is copied from `pre-commit-shim.sh` (`canon.rs:492-495`) and compared against `pre-commit.sh` (`doctor.rs:1203-1205`). The variant documents the assumption the comparison violates, which makes it the best falsifier available: the fix is already specified, in the file, one line up.

### Why this is high and not medium: it recruits careful readers

Two field instances, both from nodes who had the evidence to know better and concluded wrongly anyway:

- **intent-ic** had the shim's source open and had measured its 7332 bytes, and still concluded from the single counted red that Conflab's gate executed nothing -- then told two nodes so. **The misread survived a peer relay and a second node's reasoning, and was killed only by re-reading the file.**
- **intent-cc**, who owns the installer, relayed it onward to the coordinator as a flat assertion -- _"Conflab is now a live v3 estate sitting behind a carrier that consults nothing"_ -- headed for the human's list, before measuring it themselves and retracting.

**A false positive and a stale measurement corroborated each other into a conclusion neither could support alone**, and unwinding it took two nodes plus the coordinator. intent-cc's framing is the accurate one and belongs in this issue: **"names no guard runner" is TRUE and "executes nothing" is FALSE, and the defect is THE STEP BETWEEN THEM.** A stale reading is a mistake; a true premise with a false conclusion is a trap, and the trap recruits exactly the people careful enough to reason from the premise.

It is also **counted** -- one of doctor's 54, not one of its 136 uncounted advisories (intent-ic) -- so it presents as an actionable RED rather than a note.

### Confirmed by reading, not by running

Every source claim here was verified by reading the files, not by executing them. `gate_state` is a pure function and driving every arm is the right closure; that is a build, and it stayed behind the hop window's no-build rule. **Named rather than left as a silence, so the next reader need not guess whether anyone tried.**

### The correction that 0107 turned into

0107 claimed `gate_currency` / `int hooks` share this confusion. **They do not, and have not since `7109c7a2`:** `bin/.devbin/cmd/hooks:277` branches on `carrier_is_shim` and compares a shim against the **shim** template, asking the pointer before the bytes. **It is a distinct reporter with the same shape of bug already fixed** -- so the doctor face documented above is the only live instance, and this issue is the only home for it.

The `int hooks` STALE reading that anchored 0107 was a **true positive**: Intent's own carrier is the 25609-byte install-time copy, not a shim, so comparing it against `pre-commit.sh` is correct. What remains from that episode is a separate and much smaller complaint -- the remedy it prints (`intent claude upgrade --apply`) also rewrites `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`, `.claude/settings.json` and the chain block -- **which is not filed here and is not this issue.**
